title: Come back when you are taller
idea: A height mark on a doorframe means nothing until there is a second one above it. The page is the edge of a doorframe with one pencil mark already on it, dated the day the site began; hold still against the paint and a mark is pencilled for you with today's date, and the frame keeps it, so the piece only finishes when you return. The room beyond the door is as light or dark as your own hour.
look: warm off-white paint and brown pencil on a full-window canvas; italic Georgia caption fixed at the bottom centre, speaking to the visitor

title: Under the paint
idea: Nobody rubs out a height mark; they paint over it, so every one ever made is still on the frame, sealed between two coats. The page is the jamb from 0 seen close, and scrolling sands it back through ninety-five years of colours in widening rings, each coat giving up the initials and dates pencilled on it just before the same sanding takes them off. It ends at bare pine and the carpenter's figure for the door, and scrolling back up does not put anything back.
techniques: localStorage read from an earlier piece
look: cream and tan paint layers with wood beneath, full window; small Helvetica labels, a caption fixed at the bottom

title: A bit more
idea: A door left ajar at bedtime is a measurement too: the exact width of what a child is afraid of, agreed again every night. The same doorframe as 0 and 1, seen in the dark from the bed; you hold the door and drag it, and a small voice says more, less, a tiny bit less, until it says there, and then someone walks off down the hall. The agreed width is different each date and slightly narrower than the last, and about five years after the first mark it is nothing and you are told you can shut it.
techniques: the date as a slowly closing parameter
look: dark room with a strip of amber light, full-window canvas; italic Georgia caption low in the centre, as a spoken voice

title: No one in particular
idea: The height marks on the jamb were made one person at a time, with a name and a date; the sill was marked by everyone at once and kept nobody. The doorway of 0 to 2 handed to a surveyor: a cold measured section through the threshold, its hollow dimensioned to four decimal places, deepest off centre toward the latch because nobody walks through the middle of a door. Nothing moves; the depth is recomputed from the date and deepens by one footfall for your having opened it.
techniques: the date as a revision number
html table as a title block
look: navy line on pale grey, a measured drawing on a sheet; small monospace type, a table as title block, left-aligned

title: About three seconds
idea: The felt present is about three seconds wide, and almost nothing you make fits inside it whole. A sheet of warm paper asks you to write your name, by finger, pen or keyboard, and every mark lasts exactly three seconds, so the first letter has gone before the last is made and you never see all of it at once. A deliberate break from the doorway of 0 to 3, which was all about marks that stay.
techniques: text that answers how long you took
look: warm cream paper with dark plum ink, full-window canvas; italic serif caption low in the centre, speaking to the visitor
